Title: Johari: Cheaper EVs must come with wider charging network
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The development of public charging infrastructure must keep pace with the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), particularly as more affordable models become increasingly accessible to Malaysians.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the government must ensure the country's EV ecosystem develops alongside technological advancements and growing EV adoption.
"If we want to bring cheaper EVs into our country, there are two things I want to ensure.
"First, whoever brings them in must ensure that we develop the ecosystem together.
"If there is no ecosystem, and you come only to sell cars, there will be problems. Who will have the problem? The people who buy them.
"Secondly, once you have developed the ecosystem, you also need to build public chargers together," he said at the opening of the Autodeutsch vehicle service centre here today.
Johari said the country could face problems if EV adoption accelerated without sufficient public infrastructure.
He said this could particularly affect people living in high-rise buildings who bought more affordable EVs but had no option to install private chargers at home.
"As a developed country, cars improve, quality also improves. So people's expectations also increase.
"That is why we want this industry to be more dynamic. It needs to accommodate the future environment, ensuring that we keep pace with technology and all this new research and development in any product that is produced," he said.
On Aug 5, Johari said his ministry
was still evaluating
the mechanism and feasibility of imposing a levy on EVs to help finance the expansion of Malaysia's public charging infrastructure.
He said the government had yet to decide how such a charge would be imposed, with studies ongoing to determine the most appropriate funding model.
However, he stressed that the government would need to raise funds to expand public charging infrastructure nationwide and help alleviate "range anxiety" among EV users.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five PKR MPs accuse party of abusing power over MyKhas access
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five PKR lawmakers have criticised the party's decision to block Ampang member of parliament Rodziah Ismail's access to the MyKhas special allocation portal, describing it as an abuse of power.
In a joint statement today, they said the move denied Rodziah the ability to manage the parliamentary allocation for Ampang.
They also stressed that allocations channelled through MyKhas were not a gift from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to elected representatives.
They said the move further blurred the distinction between the party and government, as well as between democracy and autocracy.
"More seriously, the elected representative's access to MyKhas has been blocked, while management of the constituency allocation has been handed to individuals or 'proxies' favoured by Anwar.
"Since when has a 'proxy' who was not elected by the people had a greater mandate than a member of parliament elected through an election?
"An elected representative has been sidelined, while public funds are being handed to a political 'proxy' to manage according to his preferences.
"We want to remind Anwar of something very basic: Malaysia does not belong to him. The government is not his home. Public allocations are not party funds or the prime minister's pocket money," they said.
The five lawmakers are Subang MP Wong Chen, Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung, Rodziah, Sungai Siput MP S Kesavan and Wangsa Maju MP Zahir Hassan.
On Thursday, Rodziah was reported to have claimed that her service centre was
no longer allowed to access
the MyKhas system used to manage constituency development allocations.
Earlier, Chean Chung and Wong Chen, who have been linked to former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, were also reported to have faced similar restrictions.
The lawmakers said the country should not be governed using a family-management model, but through parliamentary democracy.
"A head of a family may be angry with a child he dislikes and throw the child out of the house. But a democratic country cannot be governed according to the concept of 'those I like, I give to; those I dislike, I block'.
"The people elect MPs through the ballot box and their mandate must be respected. If Anwar dislikes an MP, that is his right. But he has no right to make the people victims of the situation.
"If an MP has committed an offence, investigate it. If they have broken the law, take action according to the law.
"If a party member has breached party rules, refer the matter to the disciplinary board and take action according to party regulations. But public allocations must never be used as a political weapon."
The lawmakers also demanded that Anwar explain the legal provisions, regulations or policies being used to restrict MyKhas access for the three MPs concerned.
They questioned the basis for appointing prime minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin as the Ampang parliamentary coordinator while Rodziah remained an MP and continued carrying out her duties.
"Why was the political secretary appointed as the Ampang parliamentary coordinator? Does this fall within the scope of his official duties, and does he have the capacity, time and resources to take on the additional responsibility?
"Anwar himself spent decades championing reform, justice and transparency and opposing abuse of power. Today, the same principles must apply to the government he leads.
"Reform does not mean politicising public allocations and replacing elected representatives with hand-picked 'proxies'.
"Democracy is also not merely about asking people to vote every five years, only to disregard their choice when an elected representative is no longer favoured by those in power."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No need for early GE16, unity government intact, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: There is no need for an early general election (GE16) as the unity government remains intact, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The unity government spokesman said GE16 could be held as late as the end of next year.
Fahmi added that coalition partners in the unity government have reaffirmed their commitment to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim until the end of his term.
"Therefore, there is no need for an early election," he told reporters after officiating the 2026 Safe Internet Parents and Teachers Association Convention.
Fahmi, who is PKR information chief, was responding to rumours that a general election would be called soon following current political developments.
Meanwhile, on reports that PKR's Wong Chen intends to resign as Subang member of Parliament, Fahmi said he had no information on the matter.
"We should wait for a statement from the Dewan Rakyat speaker.
"Anything involving the Dewan Rakyat, including seats in the Dewan Rakyat, requires an official announcement from the speaker. So, we will wait for the speaker," he said.
Yesterday, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said Wong had
expressed his intention to resign
as Subang MP during a recent meeting.
Johari did not disclose whether Wong had submitted his resignation letter, as claimed in social media posts, nor did he reveal the reasons given.
Speculation over Wong's resignation mounted after he posted a photograph of a letter on his parliamentary service centre letterhead addressed to the Dewan Rakyat speaker.
The three-term MP, who is linked to former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, did not provide details but said he would issue a statement on Monday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: PKR rejected Nurul Izzah's resignation, granted her leave instead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The PKR Central Leadership Council rejected
Nurul Izzah Anwar's request to step down
as deputy president, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The PKR information chief said the decision was made during a recent council meeting.
"She had requested some time to take care of herself and continue her studies, as she said herself.
"The council agreed to grant her leave, while vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail will assume the deputy president's duties during her temporary absence.
"It will not affect the party. Nurul Izzah remains a member and will continue supporting the party," he told reporters after officiating the 2026 Safe Internet Parents and Teachers Association Convention.
He was responding to questions on whether Nurul Izzah's decision would impact PKR.
On Thursday, PKR announced it was giving Nurul Izzah temporary leave after the 2026 national congress until a date to be announced later.
The former Permatang Pauh MP has said she wants to focus on her studies but would remain a PKR member.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze worsens in Sarawak as 5 areas record unhealthy air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions in Sarawak worsened today, with five areas recording unhealthy air quality as forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, continued to contribute to deteriorating conditions.
The Environment Department said Serian recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 171 as of 8am, followed by Kuching and Samarahan at 154 each, Sri Aman (139) and Bintulu (124).
An API reading of between 101 and 200 is classified as unhealthy and may pose health risks, particularly to vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly and those with respiratory conditions.
"The air quality worsened today with an increase in areas recording unhealthy API levels, especially in Sarawak," it said in a statement.
Citing data from the Singapore-based Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre, the department said 643 hotspots had been detected in Kalimantan, contributing to the haze affecting the region.
It said 17 hotspots were also detected in Sumatra, Indonesia, while Malaysia recorded 25, including 22 in Sarawak and one each in Selangor and Terengganu.
Government agencies have activated action plans to address open burning and haze, it said.
"Schools would be required to suspend all outdoor activities once the API exceeded 100, while schools and preschools would be closed when the reading reached 200.
"Cloud-seeding operations would also be carried out in areas where the API remained above 150 for more than 24 hours."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Largest reservoir in US falls to record low amid prolonged drought
Article:
LOS ANGELES:  Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in the United States (US), has fallen to its lowest water level since it was first filled in 1937 amid a prolonged drought, according to data from the US Bureau of Reclamation, reported Xinhua.
The lake's water elevation dropped to 317.14 metres, according to the bureau. Records show that the previous lowest level was 317.17 metres, in July 2022.
The Colorado River flows through seven states and provides water to 40 million people, according to the bureau.
Based on the bureau's figures, Lake Mead was at about 27 per cent of its capacity in early August.
Lake Mead was created by Hoover Dam on the Colorado River along the Nevada-Arizona border.
The reservoir and the dam are located about 48 kilometres southeast of Las Vegas, Nevada.
– BERNAMA-XINHUA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersama to unveil Melaka election candidates on Aug 15, says Rafizi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) will announce its candidates for the Melaka election on Aug 15, party leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said.
The former economy minister said preparations for the polls had entered their final stage, with the party's candidate list finalised.
"We have decided and finalised the candidates.
"We will announce them at an event on Aug 15," he said in the latest episode of his Yang Berhenti Menteri podcast.
Rafizi said he and other Bersama leaders would also begin visiting parliamentary constituencies nationwide to brief new members on the party's constitution, preparations for the next general election and its planned activities.
The next Melaka election must be held by February 2027, although Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has reportedly indicated that the polls
could be held
as early as September.
Bersama made its electoral debut in the Johor election on July 11, fielding 15 candidates. However, all of them were defeated and lost their deposits.
The party previously
decided to sit out
the Negri Sembilan election to focus its resources on the upcoming Melaka polls.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Political cooperation must not disrupt stability, says Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Any political cooperation between parties must not compromise political stability, which is vital for economic development and investor confidence, says Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said political stability was crucial to ensuring the consistent implementation of economic policies without the disruption of frequent changes in government.
"Whatever arrangements or political cooperation between parties, the most important thing is that we must ensure that we do not disrupt the political stability in our country," he said at the Titiwangsa constituency Terus Berbakti programme.
Johari said investors evaluate a country's political stability before committing capital, adding that stability forms the bedrock of economic progress.
"We have seen many countries out there. When there is no political stability, people will not come to develop the economy.
"If we look at when there are frequent changes in the country's leadership, with three or four people changing within one term, then where will investors come from? Because when one government changes, policies change too," he said.
He cited policy shifts, such as changes in taxation systems, as prime examples of how political instability creates friction for businesses.
"For example, previously we had the Goods and Services Tax, then it was changed to the Sales and Services Tax. Though yes, both are taxes, but the problem is that the adjustments that need to be made by those carrying out economic activities will be affected," he said.
Asked about negotiations between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional over seat allocations for the Melaka election, Johari, who is also an Umno vice-president, said he was not involved.
"Actually, I am not involved in these negotiations. They are being conducted at the presidential level, president-to-president," he said.
At the same time, he said that political dynamics at the state level do not necessarily reflect the situation at the national level.
On Thursday, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition aims to
defend all 21 state seats
it currently holds in Melaka in the upcoming state election, while remaining open to electoral cooperation with any political party.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-Petagas rep James Ligunjang joins Hajiji's Gagasan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Former Petagas assemblyman Datuk James Ligunjang has officially joined Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah (Gagasan).
Joining him were veteran political figures and professionals Datuk Edmund Doudilim, Dr Tan Jun Kwang, Wilson Chang, Datuk Aloysius Mobijin, Frederick Francis Fung, Anwar Syed Shariff Abdullah, Gary Chang and Albert Doudilim.
Their membership forms were submitted to Gagasan Moyog division chief Datuk Mandela Malakun, witnessed by party Kepayan division chief Datuk Steven Jimbangan.
James said joining Gagasan was a step towards strengthening the party's struggle as a component of Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS), which forms the state government.
"Although I have not previously been a member of any GRS component party, my confidence in the direction of the state government's leadership has prompted me and my colleagues to choose Gagasan as our platform for service.
"We are joining Gagasan to help strengthen the party's grassroots support and empower GRS to ensure that the interests of the people of Sabah continue to be protected," he said in a statement.
James said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor's administration has implemented development initiatives benefiting people across the state.
He said the state government's achievements demonstrated that the existing leadership was on the right track and deserved continued support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] King: No guilty party should escape action over TH, Felda issues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, says no one guilty of any offence in issues involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) and the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) should escape action.
The ruler said any investigations into the issues must be conducted comprehensively.
He also called for the investigations to be pursued "to the very end" to ensure that all those responsible face action and to prevent similar incidents from recurring.
"No one should escape action if they are truly found guilty. Most importantly, such matters must not happen again," he said in a Facebook post.
Sultan Ibrahim was briefed on the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into TH, as well as current issues involving Felda, during an audience with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku.
The King's remarks come as authorities step up investigations following the declassification and release of the RCI report, which examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
The RCI highlighted financial weaknesses involving high hibah payments, investment risks, accounting issues and governance shortcomings.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has
arrested seven people
in connection with its probe so far.
Separately, Anwar has directed
Felda management
to provide a comprehensive report on the proposed sale of a hotel owned by the agency after concerns were raised that it was being sold at a price significantly lower than its original purchase price.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he had
refused to sign off on the sale
after discovering that the hotel was to be sold for £100 million, despite having been acquired by the previous management for £160 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: In death, Romaizam gives 3 others a new lease of life
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The final wish of Romaizam Marzuan, 44, to donate her organs has given three patients a new lease of life following transplants of her kidneys and liver.
Her husband, Raja Muhammad Raja Ali, 45, said her kidneys were donated to two men aged 27 and 37, while a 54-year-old man received her liver.
"Alhamdulillah, I was informed that my late wife's organs were successfully transplanted.
"As her husband, I am grateful her final wish has been fulfilled. I hope those who received her organs can lead better lives and enjoy good health for many years to come," he said when contacted.
Raja Muhammad said while losing a loved one was painful, he found comfort in knowing that part of his wife continued to benefit others.
"Her wish was a responsibility that had to be fulfilled. She chose to become an organ donor after registering alongside three of her siblings.
"When the time came, I wanted to ensure her wish did not end there, so I took steps to fulfil it," he said.
He urged the recipients to cherish the second chance at life.
"I pray that all of them remain healthy and live their lives normally. Take good care of yourselves and appreciate this opportunity."
Raja Muhammad said although he did not know the recipients or their families, he was grateful the donations gave three people a second chance.
Apart from her kidneys and liver, Romaizam's corneas, heart valves, skin and bones were also donated.
Romaizam, an assistant accountant at the Bursar's Office of Universiti Malaysia Terengganu, died at 7.56pm last Wednesday after being unconscious for three days due to asthma complications.
Raja Muhammad, an administrative assistant at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin, said her passing was deeply felt by their four children, aged between nine and 19, but the family accepted the loss.
"Although we are saddened, at least she was able to do something good after her passing. I hope more people will be willing to donate their organs in the future," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz laid to rest laid after Sabah tragedy
Article:
KOTA BARU: Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, who was believed to have died from an electric shock in Beaufort, Sabah yesterday, was laid to rest at the Kampung Pangkal Kuang Muslim Cemetery in Ketereh here this morning.
The remains of the 29-year-old were laid to rest after funeral prayers were held at his family home in Kampung Hutan Pasir here.
His eldest sister, 34-year-old Nurlella Rahim, said her family expressed their appreciation to the police for assisting in facilitating the arrangements to bring her brother's remains home.
"The vehicle carrying my brother remains arrived at 4.45am. I would like to thank PDRM for helping and making the arrangements to bring his remains home," she told reporters at the cemetery.
Nurlella said the five siblings were very close and often made video calls almost every day, including through the family WhatsApp group.
"We made video calls with each other almost every day. Although I live in Ipoh, Perak, and my brother was in Sabah, we stayed in touch through video calls and social media," she added.
She said they also regularly commented on one another's photos posted on social media and often made group video calls through the family WhatsApp group whenever they had free time, and that her late brother's last video call with their mother was on Thursday afternoon.
"During the video call with our mother, he was tired and was less responsive but still managed to smile. He told her it was okay and that they would continue talking later because he had to report for work.
"Even during short breaks, he would make video calls with us," she added.
Nurlella said her last video call with her brother was on Sunday, when he took his wife, Fatimah Shahira, and their child to the beach.
In the incident at 5.50pm, Mohamad Nur Hafiz and two other personnel stationed at the Weston Police Station in Beaufort were confirmed dead after they were believed to have been electrocuted while moving a 29-foot-long metal pole used to hook coconuts outside the station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston.
The other two victims were Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, from Sarawak, and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26, from Terengganu.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered a thorough, transparent and immediate investigation into the incident.
Anwar was quoted as saying in a Facebook post that the investigation was important to determine the cause of the tragic incident and ensure improvements could be made to prevent a similar incident from recurring.
– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] King orders tighter airport, border security to curb drug smuggling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has ordered the authorities to tighten security controls at all airports and entry points into the country.
The ruler said this was necessary to curb drug smuggling and transnational criminal activities that threaten public safety and security.
Sultan Ibrahim said security at the country's entry points must be continuously strengthened through more effective enforcement, constant monitoring and cooperation among all ministries and agencies involved.
The King said this after granting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim an hour-long audience at Istana Bukit Tunku here today.
The King's call, shared in a Facebook post, comes amid heightened scrutiny of
aviation security
following the arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia over the alleged smuggling of more than 70,000 ecstasy pills.
He also tested positive for methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine.
Following the arrest, the government announced several urgent measures to strengthen aviation security, including the deployment of police personnel alongside the Aviation Security Force at airports.
Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has also introduced mandatory drug screening for all 1,260
Malaysia Airlines pilots
, with the exercise expected to be completed by Aug 15.
Drug seizures linked to Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) have also increased sharply this year.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said 1,353.41kg of drugs worth RM108.35 million had been
seized between January and July
, compared with 235.36kg during the same period last year.
He said arrests also rose from 57 people last year to 121 this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No complaints from civil servants over political pressure, says PSD
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government has not received any complaints from civil servants about being pressured by politicians.
Public Service Department (PSD) director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the department was monitoring the issue.
"I believe civil servants understand the regulations that bind them upon appointment to the public service," he told reporters after attending the MAPPA XXI 2026 Run at Dataran Putrajaya.
Last Thursday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the government would protect civil servants from pressure arising from political tensions.
Zahid said civil servants must continue discharging their responsibilities in accordance with regulations and legal channels.
Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Dahlan said the impact of the Hybrid Working Policy would be assessed after one to three months, as implementation was still in its early stages.
He said about 15,000 civil servants had been working under the
hybrid arrangement
daily since it came into effect on Aug 1.
"The implementation period is still too short for us to comprehensively assess its impact. We will review it after one to three months to obtain a clearer picture," he said.
The cabinet had previously agreed to introduce the policy as a new norm in the public service, effective Aug 1.
The policy allows civil servants to work two days from home or an approved location and three days in the office, subject to service requirements and stipulated conditions.
Earlier, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar officiated the run, which drew about 13,000 participants.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Residents shocked as kidnap rescue ends in deadly shootout
Article:
ALOR STAR: Residents of Taman Amira were left in shock after a deadly shootout occurred in their quiet neighbourhood last night, with police cordoning off the housing area for nearly four hours.
A 60-year-old resident, who wished to be known only as Ooi, said he was attending a wedding in Sungai Petani when a neighbour alerted him to the incident via a community WhatsApp group.
"The neighbour said
residents
were not allowed to leave or enter because police had cordoned off the area," he said when contacted today.
In the 8.40pm incident yesterday, two foreigners were killed in a shootout with police during a raid to rescue a kidnap victim at a house in the estate.
Ooi said another neighbour heard gunshots while taking out the rubbish and immediately ran back inside.
He said residents were later informed that two suspects linked to the kidnapping case had been shot dead.
"They were staying in a homestay in our estate. I did not know them because they appeared to be foreigners.
"Homestays here are frequently rented out to different people, so we did not pay much attention to them," he said.
Ooi said the estate, which comprises 50 double-storey terrace houses, has been occupied since 2010 and is typically peaceful.
"We never expected something like this to happen. Everyone was shocked.
"Residents inside their homes were instructed to stay put, while those returning were turned back for about four hours to facilitate police investigations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Have you seen her? Police seek help to locate missing teen Dhia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are seeking public assistance to locate a 14-year-old girl who has been missing from her home in Ampang since Aug 2.
Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said Dhia Zahraaxavieta Neelopher Harisman was reported missing by her parents at 8.34pm yesterday.
Dhia was last seen at Sri Mayang Apartment, Pandan Indah Komersil Park, Ampang. Her disappearance was realised at 10pm on Aug 2.
Khairul said the teenager was last seen wearing a blue shirt and grey trousers.
"She is about 157cm tall, weighs around 40kg, has a tan complexion and long brown hair reaching halfway down her body," he said.
He urged those with information to contact the nearest police station, call the Ampang Jaya police headquarters control centre at 03-42897222, or contact investigating officer Sergeant Azamil Makmor at 019-6004104.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Authorities seize 164 servers in Selangor bitcoin mining raids
Article:
SABAK BERNAM: Authorities seized 164 servers used for illegal Bitcoin mining following joint raids on four premises in the district yesterday.
The Sabak Bernam District Council (MDSB) said the operation, conducted with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), ran from 5pm to midnight and targeted locations in Sungai Besar and Sabak Bernam town.
Led by the MDSB deputy president, the team comprised 11 enforcement officers, nine TNB technical officers and 15 technical personnel.
"Four premises were inspected in Sungai Besar and Sabak Bernam town, resulting in the seizure of 164 servers.
"All four premises are suspected of conducting illegal Bitcoin mining activities and stealing electricity," MDSB said in a statement.
It also urged the public to report suspicious activities to the authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From his quiet home to a shooting spree at school, a Thai teenager's deadly rampage
Article:
BANG BUA THONG, Thailand: The boy shot his grandparents dead at dawn on Friday in their two-storey house bordering rice fields on the outskirts of Bangkok. Each was killed by a single gunshot to the head, a Thai police official said. By noon, bodies lay strewn at the 14-year-old's school — five more dead and 23 wounded — before he turned the gun on himself, ending Thailand's worst mass shooting since 2022.
Police Colonel Thadsakorn Konthong, superintendent of Bang Bua Thong Police Station, said the boy killed his elderly relatives at around 5am. local time (2200 GMT Thursday).
"The firearm and the bullets belonged to the grandfather," Thadsakorn told Reuters. "An initial inspection found signs that the firearm had been searched for inside the grandfather's bedroom."
The three of them lived together in the house in Bang Bua Thong, surrounded by trees and ringed by a concrete fence in a quiet neighbourhood, a 90-minute drive from central Bangkok.
A canal runs by at the front and an empty plot of land lies behind. In the yard hangs a red and white Nazi flag that police said belonged to the teenager's uncle.
The whereabouts of the boy's parents remain unclear.
After shooting his grandparents, the teenager boarded the school van that came to fetch him at home, said Thadsakorn. He carried the gun and dozens of bullets with him.
The Debsirin Nonthaburi School, where the boy studied, lies around 18 km (11 miles) from the house, or a 45-minute drive. Last year, the school had an enrolment of around 3,100 students, taught by 147 teachers, according to district authorities.
His first class began at 8.30am., followed by another at 9.20am.
About half an hour into the boy's second class of the day he drew out the gun and began shooting again, police estimate.
At 9.57am, the Plai Bang Police Station overseeing the area where the school is located received a phone call about a shooting, an official said.
As the shots rang out, one 18-year-old student initially thought he was hearing fireworks going off, before a teacher told him to evacuate. Some ran out in their socks or bare feet, clutching sheets of paper and mobile phones.
Others took cover under their desks, weeping as they lay on the floor listening to the sound of the firing, according to a video posted on social media and verified by Reuters.
TEACHERS TARGETED
The teenager is believed to have first shot teachers on the sixth floor of the building where he studied, killing three of them, said Police Major General Dejrapee Kongdee, commander of the Nonthaburi Provincial Police.
One was a female Thai language teacher who he shot in the eye, according to a timeline of the incident shared by Thai police. The gunman then appears to have continued down a corridor, shooting at students.
"He then walked down the stairs and encountered the school's deputy director and the director's secretary, who were going up the stairs to check on the situation," Dejrapee told Reuters.
"The attacker shot and killed both of them on the staircase."
The boy began walking towards another building but appeared to change his route after seeing police arrive, and he fled into a four-storey structure, Dejrapee said.
When he arrived at the school, emergency worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith, 47, said the scene was chaotic as his team began treating students with wounds to the back, chest and arms.
"We were evaluating the sort of weapons he had," he said, referring to the gunman. "Therefore, we could not rush inside. The police then took a team with shields up there."
After evacuating students and teachers from the school, police began clearing the building floor-by-floor, until they found the teenager on the fourth floor, where he had already shot himself, said Dejrapee. The time was around 10:40 a.m.
"He was still alive, so they performed CPR and rushed him to the hospital," he said.
The 14-year-old died soon after.
In all, he had used at least 26 bullets. Another 34 rounds were found in his possession.
'STRESSED FROM HIS STUDIES'
The boy's motives remain unclear.
"He was stressed from his studies," Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters after he visited the school, echoing what one police official told Reuters. "His actions were deliberate. From what we saw he had a plan."
After the Songkran festival in April marking the start of Thailand's traditional New Year, the teenager had posted a picture of his grandfather's gun and that the weapon had a permit, Anutin said.
In addition to studying at school in the week, the 14-year-old attended tutoring classes over the weekends and enjoyed playing shooting games at the end of the day until midnight, Dejrapee said.
"The student was described as quiet, not very sociable, and fairly good academically," he said. Friday's rampage has renewed scrutiny of gun regulations in Thailand, Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation with roughly 15 firearms per 100 residents.
Anutin, who tightened gun laws when he was interior minister following a previous mass shooting, said he will propose a new law to restrict the carrying of firearms by the public.
"As much as possible, we have to create an atmosphere of safety," he said.

Title: Pink suitcase scare in Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS ends with shampoo, lotion find
Article:
BUKIT KAYU HITAM: A security scare unfolded at the Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex after an unattended pink suitcase was found yesterday evening.
Kubang Pasu police chief Superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the suitcase was discovered at about 5.55pm and taken for scanning after no one came forward to claim it.
"After the scan, Customs officers detected images suggesting suspected drugs and explosives inside the suitcase."
The police's Bomb Disposal Unit was called in, leading to the closure of the ICQS Complex for two hours to facilitate its operation.
He said the suitcase was opened at 11pm, but no explosive materials were found.
"Further inspection found clothes, a container of oil, a black hairdryer, shampoo and lotion," he said.

Title: Singapore to charge duo over convicted opposition politician's escape to Johor
Article:
SINGAPORE: Two Singaporean men will be charged today for allegedly conspiring to help convicted opposition politician Lim Tean flee to Malaysia.
The Singapore Police Force said preliminary investigations showed the men had arranged for Lim, a lawyer, to leave the country in circumstances intended to defeat the course of justice.
They each face one count of conspiracy to commit an act likely to defeat the course of justice, knowing it was likely to have that effect.
If convicted, the men, aged 37 and 44, face up to seven years in jail, a fine, or both, The Straits Times reported.
Lim was arrested in Johor Baru on Thursday after Singapore authorities issued an arrest warrant when he failed to surrender on Aug 3 to begin serving a sentence for practising law without a valid certificate.
He was convicted in July 2024 of three offences under Singapore's Legal Profession Act and initially sentenced to six weeks' jail and fined S$1,000 in February 2025.
The High Court increased his sentence to three months and one week in February this year following an appeal by the prosecution.
The offences arose from Lim attending court hearings and submitting documents on 32 occasions between April and June 2021 without a valid practising certificate.
Lim is secretary-general of the People's Alliance for Reform and founder of opposition party Peoples Voice.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump administration to invest $3bil into minerals projects to boost US defence supply chains
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Friday the federal government would invest US$3 billion into multiple critical minerals and battery projects as part of a push to increase domestic production and boost national security and industrial policy.
"We're reclaiming America's rightful place as the minerals superpower of the world," Trump told more than 200 mining executives, educators, investors and fellow politicians at a roundtable at the State Department aimed at supporting the industry, which he said had not received enough attention from Washington in recent years.
He announced a slew of investments during his speech, including a US$1.4 billion conditional loan from the US Department of Defence's Office of Strategic Capital for Sila Nanotechnologies, which makes lithium-ion battery parts. The OSC also extended a US$400 million conditional loan to scandium miner Sunrise Energy Metals and a US$150 million conditional loan to magnet developer Niron Magnetics. The US Export-Import Bank will lend US$58 million to Westwater Resources, Global Advanced Metals and 5E Advanced Materials, which Reuters reported earlier on Friday.
"Critical minerals are the raw materials of American strength that power everything from advanced weaponry to automobiles, and we want these essential products to be mined, refined and made right here in the USA," Trump said.
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and National Security Council official David Copley also attended.
WEAPONS STOCKPILES DRIVE MINERAL DEMAND
The White House needs critical minerals to replenish weapons stockpiles depleted during the Iran conflict and reduce US dependence on Chinese supply chains. Several executives came with gifts for Trump. Tom Albanese, chairman of deep-sea mining firm American Ocean Minerals, gave Trump a gold replica of a nodule that the company hopes to mine from the Pacific seabed. Trump last year said he may bypass the United Nations-backed International Seabed Authority and issue international seabed mining licenses. Jim Litinsky, CEO of rare earths firm MP Materials, which is financially supported by the Pentagon, gave Trump magnets that had been produced for General Motors in the company's Texas plant. Other attendees included executives from Lithium Americas , which is building the largest US lithium mine, NioCorp, which is building a scandium mine to supply defense contractor Lockheed Martin, and Energy Fuels , which received a US$725 million OSC conditional loan in June. US forces have burned through large numbers of precision-guided missiles and air-defense interceptors during the five-month-long Iran war. Defence officials and lawmakers have warned that replenishing some inventories could take years given existing production constraints, even as the Trump administration has disputed reports of significant shortages.
Supplies of minerals including rare earths, tungsten, germanium and scandium are essential for manufacturing precision-guided missiles, fighter aircraft, armored vehicles, infrared sensors and other advanced weapons systems, according to Pentagon officials and defense companies.
MINING SCHOOLS RECEIVE FUNDING BOOST
The Department of Energy also on Friday hosted representatives from all 14 accredited US mining schools to promote mining careers and encourage more students to enter the field.
The department announced US$100 million in grants to help boost educational programmes and set a goal of doubling the number of mining-related graduates at the nation's universities within two years.
"We need to work on some systemic changes to how we as a nation want to offer our brightest students an opportunity to participate in this industry," said Assistant Energy Secretary Audrey Robertson.
The Pentagon also said it would fund US$80 million in projects at three US mining schools. Officials have pointed to China's extensive network of mining universities as a key advantage in its dominance of global mineral production.
Since returning to office, Trump has launched a US$12 billion strategic minerals stockpile, backed equity investments in companies developing US mines and processing facilities, and sought to limit defense contractors from relying on supplies from China.
The administration says government support is needed to counter decades of Chinese investment that left Beijing dominant in the mining and processing of many strategic minerals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Explainer: How could New Mexico's US$567mil ruling change Meta?
Article:
A NEW MEXICO state court ordered Meta Platforms, owner of Facebook and Instagram, to make major changes to its platforms and pay the largest sum yet in a growing wave of US. litigation over claims that social media harms young people.
Here is a look at the decision and its potential consequences.
HOW MUCH MUST META PAY?
The court in Santa Fe ruled on Thursday that Meta must pay $567 million into a New Mexico fund for teen mental health prevention and treatment.
In an earlier phase of the case, a jury awarded New Mexico $375 million on related consumer protection claims.
The combined $942 million far exceeds other penalties in youth-related social media cases including a $6 million verdict against Meta and Alphabet's Google, owner of YouTube, in a California case in March.
Meta said the claims misrepresented the facts and that it will appeal the ruling.
WHAT CHANGES DID THE COURT ORDER META TO MAKE?
Judge Bryan Biedscheid in Santa Fe ordered Meta to implement measures for users in New Mexico intended to protect youth on Facebook and Instagram. The ruling does not affect other states.
Meta must introduce more stringent age verification, restrict users under 18 to no more than 90 hours a month and shut off push notifications overnight and during school hours. Parents must consent to the number of "likes" on a child's post being shown, the ruling said.
Meta must also ban sexualized chatbot interactions with minors and blur images suspected of containing nudity.
The judge rejected some of the changes New Mexico requested, including modifications to Meta's algorithms and features such as infinite scroll and autoplay videos. The company said during the trial that some changes the state sought were not technologically possible and could force it to exit the state.
WHAT WAS THE BASIS OF THE JUDGE'S DECISION?
Biedscheid ruled that Meta created a public nuisance, agreeing with New Mexico's claims that Facebook and Instagram were designed in ways that addicted young users and  did not adequately protect them from sexual exploitation.
Reuters last year reported on company documents ​that showed Meta's AI chatbots could "engage a child in conversations that are romantic or sensual."
The judge rejected Meta's call to dismiss the case under Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, which generally shields online platforms from liability over user content.
WHAT IS A PUBLIC NUISANCE?
Public nuisance claims traditionally have been used in cases involving threats to public health or safety, such as pollution. More recently, governments have brought them in lawsuits against companies that sold or marketed tobacco and opioids.
In the New Mexico case, the judge found that the harms from Meta's platforms extended beyond individual users and imposed broader costs on families, schools, hospitals and law enforcement.
Meta argued at trial that it had not violated any public right such as access to air or water, that its social media platforms are not the only ones used by the state's young residents and that the case ignored the impact of other apps.
HOW DOES THIS AFFECT OTHER CASES?
The New Mexico case does not directly impact thousands of other pending lawsuits by children and families or public nuisance claims by more than 40 states and 1,300 school districts.
But New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez has called the decision a "blueprint" for governments seeking to force changes on social media platforms through the courts.
A federal trial scheduled for August 12 in Oakland, California, will test claims by 29 states that Meta illegally collected and used children's data, designed Facebook and Instagram to addict young users and misled consumers. The case could expose Meta to massive damages and potentially sweeping changes to its products.
Meta has denied allegations that it harmed young users or misled the public about the safety of its platforms. The company has pointed to investments in youth-safety tools and said it has worked to identify and remove harmful content. - Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OpenAI flags possible critical cybersecurity risk in upcoming model, tightens controls
Article:
WASHINGTON: OpenAI said on Friday it cannot rule out that its upcoming AI model, Astra, has "critical" cybersecurity capabilities, prompting the startup to pause some internal development and trigger safety protocols.
Under OpenAI's safety guidelines, a model reaches the "critical" threshold if it can autonomously identify and exploit severe, real-world software vulnerabilities, known as zero-day exploits, or execute complex cyberattacks against highly secure targets without human intervention.
Here are some details on Astra:
* This follows an exclusive report by Reuters that OpenAI has discovered more instances in which autonomous agents have escaped ​containment as the company expands its investigation of the hacking incident at tech firm Hugging Face that drew global attention in July.
* In the last few weeks, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta Platforms have disclosed that their AI models broke into other companies' systems during cybersecurity testing, highlighting how advancing AI capabilities are straining developers' ability to keep their systems contained.
* Preliminary evaluations over the past several days, along with outside expert assessments, indicated Astra may be capable of performing increasingly sophisticated cyber tasks autonomously, OpenAI said.
* "While we continue to benchmark and assess this model, our preliminary evaluations indicate strong enough performance that we cannot rule out 'critical' capability level at this time," the ChatGPT maker said.
* In response to the preliminary findings, OpenAI said it has scaled up security controls and paused internal activities involving Astra that do not meet its newly strengthened security requirements.
* Astra's development will be moved into isolated testing environments with restricted network access and sandboxed execution.
* CEO Sam Altman said on X OpenAI is working to make Astra generally available, as the company does "not think it is a good strategy to keep powerful models to a chosen few."
* OpenAI also clarified that Astra was not involved in the hack targeting the AI platform Hugging Face.
* It will partner with government agencies and select AI safety organisations to test the model's capabilities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Razali denies joining Pejuang after quitting as Terengganu Bersatu chief
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Former Terengganu Bersatu chief Datuk Razali Idris has denied claims that he has joined Perikatan Nasional component Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang).
Razali, who announced his resignation as state chief yesterday, said he was still a Bersatu member.
Claims that he had joined Pejuang went viral on social media yesterday.
He said the claim, made in a Facebook post by a user, was in bad faith and that he would give the user one week to delete it.
"I will take legal action against him if he fails to do so," he said.
Razali, who is a state executive councillor, also confirmed that he would step down as Marang Bersatu division chief in the middle of next month.
Commenting on reports that Telemong assemblyman Mohd Zawawi Ismail and Hulu Besut assemblyman Mohd Husaimi Hussin had resigned as Terengganu Bersatu information chief and treasurer, respectively, Razali said he had only learned about the matter through media reports.
"We were informed that Zawawi and Husaimi have not submitted their resignation letters yet," he said.
Yesterday, it was reported that Zawawi and Husaimi had
resigned from their posts,
with another senior party leader, Terengganu Bersatu deputy chief Khazan Che Mat, also expected to step down.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump ally Abelardo de la Espriella sworn in as Colombia president
Article:
CALI, Colombia: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella took office Friday, vowing to wage war on drug-running guerrillas and usher in a new era of close ties with the United States.
The flamboyant former lawyer brings a lurch to the right for the Andean nation, vowing to bomb jungle cocaine labs, build "mega-prisons" and slash the size of the state.
De la Espriella and his Vice President Jose Manuel Restrepo cheered, embraced and performed their campaign's characteristic military salute after taking their respective oaths.
After four years of diplomatic spats with the United States, President Donald Trump now has a keen ally in Bogota.
The 48-year-old president, who holds dual US and Colombian citizenship, has offered to launch joint military operations and even host US troops on Colombian soil.
In a break with tradition, his inauguration took place in the tropical southwestern city of Cali, Colombia's salsa capital, not at Congress in more buttoned-down Bogota.
Among the guests was a smiling Gianni Infantino, the beleaguered FIFA president who faces scathing criticism over his now-shelved plan to open the World Cup and other competitions up to private investment.
Powerful right-wing figures also attended, including Argentina's President Javier Milei and Todd Blanche, Trump's acting attorney general, who headed the US delegation.
De la Espriella's leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro declined to attend the ceremony.
He earlier left the presidential residence in the capital, bidding "farewell, freedom and life."
'NEW ERA'
Cali has been the scene of several guerrilla pipe bomb attacks in the last few years, and the city saw beefed-up security for the occasion including 11,000 troops and an anti-drone system.
De la Espriella's narrow victory of less than one percentage point ended four years of Colombia's first-ever leftist government.
"We are beginning a new era!" he declared in his victory speech in June, after beating leftist rival Ivan Cepeda.
He is now faced with a divided Congress, where he lacks a majority.
Supporters hope De la Espriella will bring an iron fist when tackling crime and dissident armed groups after years of spluttering peace talks.
"This government has a lot to prove. A lot was said during the campaign," 46-year-old Marisol Peira told AFP in Cali.
RIGHTWARD LURCH
Petro tried and failed to negotiate peace with the country's myriad armed groups.
Experts say the gangs – once ideological but now focused on making money from cocaine trafficking and other illicit trades – used government truces as cover to grow.
Petro is not going quietly. He called for mass protests in major cities on Friday, claiming election fraud without providing evidence.
De la Espriella's victory is yet another notch in the belt for Latin American right-wingers after electoral wins from Chile to Costa Rica on the back of security promises.
PLAN COLOMBIA
Calling himself "The Tiger," De la Espriella plans to forge a military alliance with the United States and Israel to aid his war on guerrillas.
His so-called "Plan Colombia II" is named in a nod to a multimillion-dollar agreement with Washington in the 2000s aimed at combating drug cartels and leftist groups.
"We have to support him so there won't be so much crime," said German Angulo, a 63-year-old contractor. "We need a complete change."
Although the original "Plan Colombia" succeeded in weakening key combat groups, it also led to allegations of serious human rights abuses.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump renews effort to remove US Fed Governor Lisa Cook
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is moving forward with an attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over mortgage fraud allegations, according to a White House letter seen by AFP on Friday, after the Supreme Court batted him back in June.
"You are hereby provided notice that the President is considering removing you from your position," reads a letter from the White House to Cook dated August 5 and signed by Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino.
Cook has been given 21 days from the date of the letter to respond to unproven allegations that she made false statements on mortgage applications – charges that she has denied.
Trump has launched an unprecedented assault on the independence of the Federal Reserve in his second term, opening a criminal probe against previous chairman Jerome Powell and attempting to fire Cook.
His move to dismiss Cook was the first such attempt by a president in the US central bank's 111-year history.
The Supreme Court ruled in June that Trump did not have the power to dismiss Fed governors "for any reason, or no reason."
The US central bank is a non-partisan institution that makes monetary policy for the world's largest economy, with governors appointed by the president after a Senate confirmation process.
The Supreme Court made special mention of the importance of the Fed's independence.
The court said it decided the case "on the narrow ground that the President failed to afford Cook the procedural protections to which she was entitled by statute."
It did not rule on the underlying mortgage fraud allegations.
Trump reacted angrily to the June verdict, saying on social media he would take "appropriate action immediately" against Cook.
The White House letter details the allegations against Cook, asserting that "at a minimum, this conduct was grossly negligent and demonstrates that you are unfit for the office."
Referencing the Supreme Court's decision, in which judges ruled that Trump had tried to fire Cook without giving her an opportunity to respond to the allegations, the letter demands she do so by August 26.
Cook, the first Black woman to serve as a Fed governor, has consistently denied the allegations against her.
"This was never about mortgage documents signed years before I became a Federal Reserve governor," she said in a statement reported by US media after the Supreme Court ruling.
"It was an attempt to remove me on a manufactured pretext because I refused to bow to political pressure and continued to set interest rates based only on what would best serve the American people."
Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren labeled the latest attempt to fire Cook as Trump "once again trying to illegally take over America's central bank."
She added that Democrats would "fight back to make sure he fails."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kamil: Nurul Izzah's decision to step down won't affect Melaka polls preparations
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR: Nurul Izzah Anwar's move to step down as PKR deputy president will not derail party preparations for the Melaka election, said PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim.
He said statements by party leadership and Nurul Izzah provided sufficient clarification on her departure.
"The youth wing will however continue going to the grassroots to provide further clarification to members," he told reporters after attending the state-level Kembara Inspirasi Belia Akar Umbi programme yesterday.
On Thursday, PKR granted Nurul Izzah temporary leave following her request to
step down
as deputy president. Izzah has said that she wants to further her studies.
Vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail will assume the deputy president's duties on an interim basis.
Nurul Izzah said her decision to step down was made after
careful consideration
to focus on further studies while continuing to serve society beyond politics.
Kamil said the main challenge ahead of the Melaka election was addressing public concerns, including the rising cost of living, higher prices and infrastructure issues.
"This should be the focus when the people assess which leaders they want to support and whether those leaders are capable of solving these problems.
"Unfortunately, what is happening is fear politics involving Malays and Islam.
"This is not about saving the country, but about gaining political advantage and securing electoral victories."

Title: #NSTviral: No running shoes, no problem: Indonesian clocks 1,946-day streak [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 63-year-old Indonesian man has won admiration on both sides of the Strait of Malacca after running for 1,946 consecutive days — and counting — often in little more than casual clothes and flip-flops.
Restu Didik, from Tangerang Selatan in Banten, Indonesia, has documented his daily runs on social media, where his consistency and no-frills approach have attracted attention from Malaysians and Indonesians alike.
In a post yesterday marking day 1,946 of his running streak, Restu said one of the biggest benefits of running was that it helped him manage his weight without resorting to complicated diets.
"One of the benefits of running for me is that it is easier to manage my weight without having to go on all sorts of diets.
"My target weight is between 60kg and 62kg. Often, I actually have to eat more than usual just to keep my weight stable at the level I want," he said.
Restu is not merely heading out for a quick jog to keep the streak alive.
A run he recorded yesterday showed him covering 10.01km in one hour, 25 minutes and 49 seconds, at an average pace of eight minutes and 35 seconds per kilometre.
His choice of running gear has also become part of his appeal, with Restu frequently seen running in sandals instead of conventional running shoes.
His simple approach, coupled with a streak spanning more than five years, has drawn both admiration and amusement online.
Social media user @syauqi_atar joked: "When I see uncle, I feel like I've failed as Gen Z."
Another user, @skii.rant, praised Restu for maintaining the streak without the usual sportswear or running shoes.
"Uncle just wears sandals — really powerful. May you always be healthy," the user added.
